text:
Priya R: Quick proposal: introduce a small "access-orchestrator" service between the UI and the query layer to own routing + policy resolution for dashboard requests. It would: compute tile-level visibility, synthesize short-lived downscoped tokens for tile fetches, and choose the target query pool (fast/slow/tiling).

Jon K: Curious about perf impact — adding another hop worries me for interactive dashboards. Any numbers?

Priya R: I measured a rough prototype: cold path adds ~3–6ms (policy eval + token mint), warm path with local policy cache ~0.8–1.5ms. We save repeated DB auth lookups and can batch policy checks per dashboard render. Net effect for typical dashboard load is +1ms median, sometimes -5–10ms for heavy multi-tile pages because query layer avoids redundant auth.

Maya S: Telemetry question: will we preserve trace context? We must keep distributed traces intact and still attribute cost to tenant/model route.

Priya R: Yes — the orchestrator forwards the incoming trace id and injects a route metadata header (x-rw-route) so dashboards, query nodes, and billing can reconstruct. Also annotates whether token was downscoped (useful for SLO / audit).

Eli G: Alternative: keep policy checks in the query layer but add a shared policy cache + a lightweight router in the UI. Pros: avoids extra network hop. Cons: duplicates routing policy in many query variants, harder to evolve routing rules.

Sam L: From an ops and rollout POV I prefer a central orchestrator. Easier to canary: route subset of tenants through new path, compare latency and error rate, and fallback to legacy flow.

Jon K: How about failure modes? If orchestrator is down we mustn't break UI — need fast fallback that still enforces RBAC but maybe without downscoped tokens.

Priya R: Agreed. Plan: orchestrator returns an explicit header with token+route. UI falls back to client-side direct call to query layer with a short-lived UI token that has the same RBAC but no per-tile downscoping. Fallback is less optimal for least-privilege but safe.

Eli G: Policy complexity: tiling introduces per-tile visibility (row/col) — do we push that calculation to the orchestrator or keep it in query? My vote: orchestrator computes a shallow visibility mask (which tiles are allowed) and query retains final enforcement. That minimizes repeated tile policy computation while keeping enforcement local to data plane.

Priya R: Exactly. Orchestrator will publish a compact tile bitmap and a signed token claiming the visibility set. Query still validates token signature before serving tile content.

Sam L: Rollout steps (suggested):
1) feature flag on UI to enable orchestrator routing per-tenant
2) orchestrator runs in passive mode (compute decision but return "continue-legacy" header) for 1 week to measure
3) enable optimistic routing for 10% tenants 
4) increase to 50% with performance guard rails (99p latency, error rate thresholds)
5) mandatory cutover after 2 weeks of stability

Priya R: I'll draft the RFC with API contract. Pseudo-config for the router rules (WIP):
```
routes:
  - name: fast-tiles
    match: "/dash/*/tiles?type=inline"
    policy: tenant-role->tile-read
    target: query-fast
    sign_downscope: true
  - name: slow-exec
    match: "/dash/*/exec"
    policy: tenant-role->exec
    target: query-slow
    sign_downscope: false
```

Maya S: Need to include telemetry knobs: sample 100% traces for canary tenants, add metric for "orchestrator_e2e_ms" and "downscope_mint_errors". Also a gauge for cache hit rate.

Jon K: One more thing — authz model. We should map existing role -> permission table to a simpler bitmask the orchestrator can evaluate quickly. Avoid full SQL-style policies in hot path.

Priya R: Good call. I'll add a migration step to precompute role-bitmasks in our config store and a compatibility layer for custom org policies.

deploy-bot: New service "access-orchestrator" repo created under infra/team, CI pipeline scaffolded. :rocket:

Sam L: Action items: Priya to RFC, Eli to sketch query validation (token signature + bitmap), Jon to run microbench tests on prototype, Maya to add observability checklist. We'll sync Thu 11am. :thumbsup:
